result:
The proposed answer is almost certainly wrong, because the problem asks for a formula in terms of both s and d, and d−1 is independent of s.

The space of morphisms of τ-degree at most s is an F_q-vector space. It is closed under left multiplication by φ_a for a ∈ F_q[T], and deg_τ(φ_a ∘ f) = 2·deg_T(a) + deg_τ(f) because the modules have rank 2. So the space cannot be bounded by a constant. Morphisms over F̄_𝔭 between supersingular modules form a finitely generated module of rank 4 over F_q[T] (an order in a quaternion algebra over F_q(T)). Filtering a rank-4 module by τ-degree gives dimension growing roughly like 2s plus a constant. So m_s should grow linearly in s, not stay at d−1.

The "stabilization" in the problem therefore cannot refer to m_s itself becoming constant. The proposed justification (τ-degrees 0, …, d−2, each contributing a one-dimensional piece) is also unsupported. I did not derive the exact linear formula, though a value of the form 2s − d + 3 would agree with d−1 at s = d−2. That is only a consistency check, not a verified result.

VERDICT: REJECT
